title: Arakhin 12
description: Do libations brought on their own need the Levites’ song? Rabbi Yosei’s baraita on the day the Temple fell leads into a long count of exiles, Sabbatical Years and Jubilees, from Nebuchadnezzar’s reign to Ezekiel’s “twenty-fifth year,” and on to the priestly watches that returned from Babylonia.
topics: 🍷 Libations brought by themselves: do they require song?

a1.he: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: נְסָכִים הַבָּאִים בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָן טְעוּנִין שִׁירָה אוֹ אֵין טְעוּנִין שִׁירָה? כֵּיוָן דְּאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן: ״מִנַּיִן שֶׁאֵין אוֹמְרִים שִׁירָה אֶלָּא עַל הַיַּיִן״ — אָמְרִינַן, אוֹ דִלְמָא עַל אֲכִילָה וּשְׁתִיָּה אָמְרִינַן, אַשְּׁתִיָּיה לְחוֹדַהּ לָא אָמְרִינַן?

a2.he: תָּא שְׁמַע: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: מְגַלְגְּלִין זְכוּת לְיוֹם זַכַּאי וְכוּ׳.

a3.he: הַאי שִׁירָה מַאי עֲבִידְתַּיהּ? אִילֵּימָא דְּעוֹלַת חוֹבָה, מִי הֲוָה? בְּשִׁבְעָה עָשָׂר בְּתַמּוּז בָּטַל הַתָּמִיד! וְאֶלָּא דְּעוֹלַת נְדָבָה — וְהָא תָּנֵי רַב מָרִי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב כָּהֲנָא דְּלָא צְרִיכָא! אֶלָּא לָאו דִּנְסָכִין.

a4.he: אָמַר רָבָא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב אָשֵׁי: וְתִסְבְּרָא?! שִׁירָה דְּיוֹמֵיהּ ״לַה׳ הָאָרֶץ וּמְלוֹאָהּ״, ״וַיָּשֶׁב עֲלֵיהֶם אֶת אוֹנָם״ בְּשִׁירָה דְּאַרְבְּעָה בְּשַׁבָּא הוּא! אֶלָּא אִילְיָיא בְּעָלְמָא הוּא דִּנְפַל לְהוּ בְּפוּמַּיְיהוּ.

a5.he: וְהָא ״עוֹמְדִים עַל דּוּכָנָן״ קָתָנֵי! כִּדְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ, דְּאָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: אוֹמֵר שִׁירָה שֶׁלֹּא עַל הַקׇּרְבָּן. אִי הָכִי, בִּנְסָכִים נָמֵי לֵימָא! נָפֵיק מִינֵּיהּ חוּרְבָּא.

a6.he: גּוּפָא, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: מְגַלְגְּלִין זְכוּת לְיוֹם זַכַּאי וְכוּ׳.

a7.he: בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה, בְּמוֹצָאֵי שְׁבִיעִית מִי מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ? וְהָכְתִיב: ״בְּעֶשְׂרִים וְחָמֵשׁ שָׁנָה לְגָלוּתֵנוּ, בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה בֶּעָשׂוֹר לַחֹדֶשׁ, בְּאַרְבַּע עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה אַחַר אֲשֶׁר הוּכְּתָה הָעִיר״! אֵיזוֹ הִיא שָׁנָה שֶׁרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה בֶּעָשׂוֹר לַחֹדֶשׁ? הֱוֵי אוֹמֵר: זֶה יוֹבֵל.

a8.he: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ בְּחַד בְּשָׁבוּעַ חֲרוּב, מֵחַד בְּשָׁבוּעַ לְחַד בְּשָׁבוּעַ — תַּמְנֵי, לְחַד בְּשָׁבוּעַ אַחֲרִינָא — חֲמֵשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה הָוְויָין.

a9.he: אָמַר רָבִינָא: בְּאַרְבַּע עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה אַחַר שָׁנָה שֶׁהוּכְּתָה הָעִיר.

a10.he: אִי הָכִי, ״בְּעֶשְׂרִים וְחָמֵשׁ שָׁנָה״? עֶשְׂרִים וָשֵׁשׁ הָוְיָין! דְּאָמַר מָר: גָּלוּ בְּשֶׁבַע, גָּלוּ בִּשְׁמוֹנֶה.

a11.he: גָּלוּ בִּשְׁמוֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה, גָּלוּ בִּתְשַׁע עֶשְׂרֵה.

a12.he: מִשַּׁב וְעַד תַּמְנֵי סְרֵי — חַד סְרֵי, וַחֲמֵשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה — עֶשְׂרִים וְשֵׁית הָוְיָא!

a13.he: אָמַר לָךְ רָבִינָא: וּלְדִידָךְ מִי נִיחָא? מִכְּדֵי גָּלוּ נָמֵי בִּתְשַׁע עֶשְׂרֵה, מִשַּׁב וְעַד תְּשַׁסְרֵי — תַּרְתֵּי סְרֵי, וְאַרְבַּע סְרֵי — עֶשְׂרִים וְשֵׁית הָוְיָין! אֶלָּא מַאי אִית לָךְ לְמֵימַר? לְבַר מִשַּׁתָּא דִּגְלוֹ בַּהּ. לְדִידִי נָמֵי — לְבַר מִשַּׁתָּא דִּגְלוֹ בַּהּ.

a15.he: מִי סָבְרַתְּ שָׁלֹשׁ גָּלִיּוֹת הֲוַי? גָּלוּ בְּשֶׁבַע לְכִיבּוּשׁ יְהוֹיָקִים, שֶׁהִיא שְׁמוֹנֶה לִנְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר, גָּלוּ בִּשְׁמוֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה לְכִיבּוּשׁ יְהוֹיָקִים, שֶׁהִיא תְּשַׁע עֶשְׂרֵה לִנְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר.

a16.he: דְּאָמַר מָר: שָׁנָה רִאשׁוֹנָה כִּיבֵּשׁ נִינְוֵה,

b3.he: וּשְׁנִיָּה בְּמוֹצָאֵי שְׁבִיעִית מִי מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ? מִכְּדִי בַּיִת שֵׁנִי כַּמָּה קָם? אַרְבַּע מְאָה וְעֶשְׂרִים. אַרְבַּע מְאָה — תְּמָנְיָא יוֹבֵלֵי, אַרְבֵּסְרֵי — תְּרֵי שָׁבוּעַ, פָּשׁוּ לְהוּ שֵׁית, הָוֵה לֵיהּ בְּשִׁיתָּא בַּשָּׁבוּעַ.

b4.he: הָא מַנִּי? רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא, דְּאָמַר: ״שְׁנַת חֲמִשִּׁים עוֹלָה לְכָאן וּלְכָאן״, אַיְיתִי תְּמָנְיָא מִתְּמָנְיָא יוֹבֵלֵי, וְהָנֵי שֵׁית — הָוֵי אַרְבֵּיסַר, אִישְׁתְּכַח דִּבְמוֹצָאֵי שְׁבִיעִית חֲרוּב.

b5.he: אִי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה לָא מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ! דְּתַנְיָא: שִׁבְעָה עָשָׂר יוֹבֵלוֹת מָנוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל מִשֶּׁנִּכְנְסוּ לָאָרֶץ וְעַד שֶׁיָּצְאוּ, וְאִי אַתָּה יָכוֹל לוֹמַר מִשָּׁעָה שֶׁנִּכְנְסוּ מָנוּ, שֶׁאִם אַתָּה אוֹמֵר כֵּן — נִמְצָא בַּיִת חָרֵב בִּתְחִילַּת יוֹבֵל, וְאִי אַתָּה מוֹצֵא ״בְּאַרְבַּע עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה אַחַר אֲשֶׁר הֻכְּתָה הָעִיר״.

b6.he: אֶלָּא צֵא מֵהֶם שֶׁבַע שֶׁכִּיבְּשׁוּ, וְשֶׁבַע שֶׁחִילְּקוּ, וְאַתָּה מוֹצֵא ״בְּאַרְבַּע עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה אַחַר אֲשֶׁר הֻכְּתָה הָעִיר״.

b7.he: וְאִי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, אַיְיתִי שַׁבְסְרֵי מִשַּׁבְסְרֵי יוֹבֵלֵי, שְׁדִי אַהָנֵי — הֲוָה לֵיהּ בִּתְלָתָא בַּשָּׁבוּעַ!

b8.he: הָנָךְ שְׁנֵי דְּאַגְלִינְהוּ סַנְחֵרִיב, עַד דַּאֲתָא יִרְמְיָה אַהְדְּרִינְהוּ — לָא קָחָשֵׁיב לְהוּ.

b9.he: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: לְעוֹלָם רַבָּנַן, וְכִי קָתָנֵי ״וְכֵן בַּשְּׁנִיָּה״ — אַשְּׁאָרָא.

b10.he: הָכִי נָמֵי מִסְתַּבְּרָא, דְּאִי לָא תֵּימָא הָכִי, מִשְׁמַרְתּוֹ שֶׁל יְהוֹיָרִיב בַּשְּׁנִיָּה מִי הֲוַאי?

b11.he: וְהָתַנְיָא: אַרְבַּע מִשְׁמָרוֹת עָלוּ מִן הַגּוֹלָה — יְדַעְיָה וְחָרִים פַּשְׁחוּר וְאִימֵּר, עָמְדוּ נְבִיאִים שֶׁבֵּינֵיהֶם וְחִלְּקוּם לְעֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבַּע מִשְׁמָרוֹת, בְּלָלוּם וּנְתָנוּם בַּקַּלְפִּי, בָּא יְדַעְיָה וְנָטַל חֶלְקוֹ וְחֵלֶק חֲבֵירָיו שֵׁשׁ,

messages.text: Continued from 11b: Rav Mari, son of Rav Kahana, derived from “over your burnt offerings, and over the sacrifices of your peace offerings” that song accompanies only an offering with a set time, so a voluntary burnt offering does not require song.

With regard to libations that are brought by themselves, without an animal offering, do they require song on the part of the Levites as the libations are poured on the altar, or do they not require song?
messages.lead: § A dilemma was raised before the Sages:

notes.he: כגון שהביאו היום קרבן ציבור ולא הביאו נסכים עמו והביאום למחר דאמר מר (מנחות דף מד:) מנחתם ונסכיהם בלילה מנחתם ונסכיהם אפי' למחר:
notes.en: Libations that are brought by themselves: for example, they brought a communal offering today and did not bring the libations with it, and they brought them the next day. As the Master said (Menaḥot 44b): “Their meal offering and their libations,” even at night; “their meal offering and their libations,” even the next day.

notes.dh: נסכים הבאים בפני עצמן טעונין שירה או לאו
notes.he: פי' נסכים מקרבן ציבור שלא הקריבו ביומו ולמחר מקריבין כדדרשי' (מנחות דף מד:) ומנחתם עד עשרה ימים וליכא לפרושי אם התנדב אדם מנחת נסכים דאפי' הביאו קרבן חובה קרבנו אין טעון נסכים ומיירי ודאי שמקריבה ביום אבל מקריבה בלילה [הא] א"ר אלעזר מה כפרה ביום אף שירה ביום:
notes.en: Libations that are brought by themselves, do they require song or not: meaning, the libations of a communal offering that were not offered on its day, and are offered the next day, as we expound (Menaḥot 44b): “And their meal offering,” even up to ten days. One cannot explain it as a case where a person donated a meal offering of libations, for even when they bring an obligatory offering, his [an individual’s] offering does not require libations [the sense appears to be: song]. And it certainly speaks of offering them by day; but offering them at night, Rabbi Elazar has already said: Just as atonement is by day, so song is by day.

notes.he: נסכין הבאין בפני עצמן כדאמרינן במס' מנחות (דף מד) האומר הרי עלי יין לא יפחות מג' לוגין:
notes.en: Libations that come by themselves: as we say in tractate Menaḥot (44): One who says, “I take upon myself [to bring] wine,” may not bring less than three log.

messages.text: From where is it derived that one recites a song of praise in the Temple only over wine?
messages.lead: The Gemara explains the sides of the dilemma: Should it be assumed that, since Shmuel bar Naḥmani says that Rabbi Yonatan says:

messages.text: Then it can be inferred that we recite songs whenever wine is poured on the altar? Or perhaps we recite songs only upon the eating and drinking of the altar, i.e., when both an animal offering is burnt and a libation is also poured upon the altar, but upon the drinking of the altar alone, we do not recite songs.

notes.he: קרבן ונסכים:
notes.en: Eating and drinking: the offering and the libations.

notes.he: [או דלמא] על אכילה ושתיה דמזבח על זבח הקרב עם נסכיו:
notes.en: [Or perhaps] over the eating and drinking of the altar: over an offering that is sacrificed together with its libations.

messages.text: The Gemara seeks to resolve the dilemma through a baraita cited earlier. Come and hear:
A fortunate matter is brought about on an auspicious day, and a deleterious matter on an inauspicious day, e.g., the Ninth of Av, on which several tragedies have already occurred.

As the Sages said: When the Temple was destroyed for the first time, that day was the Ninth of Av; and it was the conclusion of Shabbat; and it was the year after a Sabbatical Year; and it was the week of the priestly watch of Jehoiarib; and the priests and Levites were standing on their platform and singing the verse: “And He brought upon them their own iniquity, and He will cut them off in their own evil.”

verse.he: וַיָּשֶׁב עֲלֵיהֶם ׀ אֶת־אוֹנָם וּבְרָעָתָם יַצְמִיתֵם יַצְמִיתֵם יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵינוּ׃ {פ}
verse.en:
Their evil will be made to recoil upon them,
through their own wickedness they will be annihilated;
the ETERNAL our God will annihilate them.

messages.text: This song, what was its purpose? If we say that it accompanied an obligatory burnt offering, was there any obligatory communal burnt offering sacrificed at that time? The daily offering had ceased to be brought on the seventeenth of Tammuz, three weeks before the Ninth of Av.
messages.quote: the priests and Levites were standing on their platform and singing

messages.text: Rather, it would seem that this song accompanied a voluntary burnt offering.
But didn’t Rav Mari, son of Rav Kahana, teach that a voluntary burnt offering does not require song?

notes.dh: והא תני רב מרי בריה דרב כהנא
notes.he: לעיל דאין עולת נדבה טעונה שיר שהרי אין זמנה קבוע:
notes.en: But didn’t Rav Mari, son of Rav Kahana, teach: above [11b], that a voluntary burnt offering does not require song, since its time is not fixed.

messages.text: Rather, is it not the case that the song accompanied libations brought without an animal offering? This would prove that the Levites sing when a wine libation is brought, even without an animal offering.

notes.he: [והתני רב מרי על עולותיכם וגו' אלא לאו דנסכין [הבאין] בפני עצמן דבטל תמיד]:
notes.en: [“But didn’t Rav Mari teach: ‘Over your burnt offerings…’? Rather, is it not about libations [brought] by themselves?” (Editor’s note: It seems something is missing here, and it should read: One cannot say that they recited song over the libations of the daily offering, since the daily offering had already ceased.) “Since the daily offering had ceased.”]

messages.text: And can you understand that this song was recited over any offering? The song of the day for Sunday, which is when the baraita says that the Temple was destroyed, is the psalm beginning with the verse: “A psalm of David. The earth is the Lord’s, and the fullness thereof.” And yet the verse that the baraita says that the Levites were singing: “And He brought upon them their own iniquity,” is in the song for Wednesday, not the song for Sunday.
messages.quote: And He brought upon them their own iniquity

verse.he: לְדָוִד מִזְמוֹר לַיהֹוָה הָאָרֶץ וּמְלוֹאָהּ תֵּבֵל וְיֹשְׁבֵי בָהּ׃
verse.en:
Of David. A psalm.
The earth is GOD’s and all that it holds,
the world and its inhabitants.

notes.he: דלשם שירה אמרו באחד בשבת:
notes.en: And can you understand it: that they were saying it as song on Sunday?

notes.he: ואי נמי נסכים הבאים בפני עצמן טעונים שירה היינו שיר של יום שמביאין אותו ולא שיר שהיה ראוי ביום הבאת קרבן:
notes.en: And can you understand it? The song of the day is “The earth is the Lord’s”: and even if libations brought by themselves do require song, that would be the song of the day on which they are brought, and not the song that was fitting for the day the offering itself was brought.

messages.text: Rather, it was merely a portentous lamentation that came into their mouths, not a song recited over an offering. Consequently, no proof can be offered from this baraita.
But isn’t it taught in the baraita that the Levites were standing on their platform near the altar, which is the place where they sing to accompany offerings?
This can be explained in accordance with the opinion of Reish Lakish.
The Levites are permitted to recite a song on the platform even when it is not for an offering.
If so, let them also recite a song for libations that are brought without an animal offering, even if that is not required.
messages.quote: recite a song on the platform even when it is not for an offering

notes.he: אי הכי כיון דאי בעי מצי למימר שירה שלא על הקרבן לימא נמי אנסכים:
notes.en: If so: since they could, if they wished, recite song not over an offering, let them recite it over libations too.

messages.text: This could result in a mishap, as the Levites might assume that just as singing for libations which are brought without an animal offering is optional, so too, singing for libations that accompany an animal offering is also optional.

notes.he: דאתי למימר כי היכי דנסכים הבאים בפני עצמן רשות נסכים הבאין עם הקרבן נמי רשות:
notes.en: It could result in a mishap: for people would come to say that just as libations brought by themselves are optional, so too libations brought with the offering are optional.

notes.he: דסברי דדינא דנסכין לא מצו קריבי אלא ע"י שיר [ואי ליכא לויים לא הוו מקרבי להו ואינהו לא בעו שיר:
notes.en: It could result in a mishap: for they would think that the law of libations is that they may be offered only with song, [and if there were no Levites they would not offer them; yet these do not require song.

messages.text: § The Gemara discusses the matter itself cited in the baraita.

A fortunate matter is brought about on an auspicious day, and a deleterious matter on an inauspicious day. As the Sages said: When the Temple was destroyed for the first time, that day was the Ninth of Av; and it was the conclusion of Shabbat; and it was the year after a Sabbatical Year.

Can you find such a possibility, that when the Temple was destroyed for the first time it was in the year after a Sabbatical Year? But isn’t it written in a verse that Ezekiel experienced a prophecy “in the twenty-fifth year of our captivity, at the beginning of the year, on the tenth day of the month, in the fourteenth year after the city was smitten”?
messages.quote: it was the year after a Sabbatical Year

verse.he: בְּעֶשְׂרִים וְחָמֵשׁ שָׁנָה לְגָלוּתֵנוּ בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה בֶּעָשׂוֹר לַחֹדֶשׁ בְּאַרְבַּע עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה אַחַר אֲשֶׁר הֻכְּתָה הָעִיר בְּעֶצֶם ׀ הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה הָיְתָה עָלַי יַד־יְהֹוָה וַיָּבֵא אֹתִי שָׁמָּה׃
verse.en: In the twenty-fifth year of our exile, the fourteenth year after the city had fallen, at the beginning of the year, the tenth day of the month—on that very day—GOD’s hand came upon me, and it brought me there.

notes.he: גלות יהויכין והחרש והמסגר ויחזקאל היה מהם:
notes.en: Of our captivity: the exile of Jehoiachin and the craftsmen and the smiths; and Ezekiel was among them.

notes.he: לגלות יכניה ארבע עשרה שנה אחרי אשר הוכתה העיר לגלות צדקיה:
notes.en: “In the twenty-fifth year of our captivity”: of the exile of Jeconiah; “fourteen years after the city was smitten”: of the exile of Zedekiah.

messages.text: Which is the year when the beginning of the year is on the tenth of the month? You must say that this is referring to the Jubilee, which begins on Yom Kippur, the tenth of Tishrei.

notes.he: ראש השנה שלה ביום הכפורים דתוקעין ב"ד בשופר ונפטרים עבדים לבתיהן ושדות חוזרות לבעליהן ואז נראית שהיא יובל. אלמא שנת היובל הוה בשנת י"ד לחורבן הבית וקס"ד בהדי שתא דחורבן קאמר ויובל הוא לעולם במוצאי שביעית דשנת מ"ט שביעית היא:
notes.en: Jubilee: its New Year is on Yom Kippur, when the court sounds the shofar, slaves go free to their homes and fields return to their owners, and then it becomes evident that it is a Jubilee. Evidently the Jubilee Year was in the fourteenth year from the destruction of the Temple; and it was assumed that he means counting together with the year of the destruction. And the Jubilee always falls in the year after a Sabbatical Year, since the forty-ninth year is a Sabbatical Year.

notes.he: שראש השנה שלה בעשור דלא אשכח שיום ר"ה דהוי בעשור אלא יובל ביוה"כ אלמא בשנת י"ד יובל הוא:
notes.en: For its New Year is on the tenth: for you do not find a New Year day that falls on the tenth except the Jubilee, on Yom Kippur. Evidently, in the fourteenth year it was a Jubilee.

messages.text: But if it enters your mind to say that the Temple was destroyed in the first year of the Sabbatical cycle, it is impossible that the Jubilee, which follows a Sabbatical Year, occurred on the fourteenth year after the destruction of the Temple:

notes.he: היכי משכחת לה י"ד לבהדי דתיהוי במוצאי שביעית אחד בשבוע וכו':
notes.en: And if it enters your mind that it was destroyed in the year after the Sabbatical Year: how can you find fourteen [years to the Jubilee], counting together [with the year of destruction], if it was in the year after a Sabbatical Year, the first of the cycle, and so on.

messages.text: Counting from the first year of the Sabbatical cycle to the next first year of the Sabbatical cycle, one arrives at year eight. If one continues to count to the first year of yet another Sabbatical cycle, it is the fifteenth year after the year of the destruction of the Temple, not the fourteenth year.

notes.he: למפרע קחשיב ט"ו שנה:
notes.en: From the first of the cycle to the first of the cycle: he counts fifteen years backward.

notes.he: ואי ס"ד בחד בשבוע חרב מחד בשבוע עד לחד בשבוע תליתאי הרי ט"ו הוו ולא איקלע יובל עד שנת ט"ו אלא ש"מ מדאמר קרא בי"ד שנה ותו לא וההיא הוה יובל לא משכחת לה דחרב הבית אלא בשנה שניה לשבוע ואישתכח דאתא יובל בי"ד שנה:
notes.en: And if it enters your mind that it was destroyed in the first of the cycle: from the first of the cycle to the first of the third cycle makes fifteen, and the Jubilee would not arrive until the fifteenth year. Rather, conclude from it: since the verse says “in the fourteenth year” and no more, and that was a Jubilee, you cannot find it unless the Temple was destroyed in the second year of the cycle, and then the Jubilee arrives in the fourteenth year.

messages.text: The meaning of the verse is that it was in the fourteenth year after the year that the city was smitten. The year of the destruction is not counted as year one of the fourteen years; rather, year one was the following year. The destruction took place in the thirty-sixth year of the Jubilee cycle, and therefore the Jubilee occurred fourteen years later.
messages.quote: in the fourteenth year after the city was smitten

notes.he: וכי חשבת ט"ו שנים משנת היובל למפרע משכחת חורבן במוצאי שביעית שהיא שנת ל"ו למנין יובל זה:
notes.en: After the year: and when you count fifteen years backward from the Jubilee Year, you find the destruction in the year after a Sabbatical Year, which is the thirty-sixth year in the count of this Jubilee.

notes.he: בי"ד אחר שנה שהוכתה העיר [דהיינו] בשנת ט"ו לחורבן אז היה יובל:
notes.en: Ravina said: “in the fourteenth after the year the city was smitten,” [that is,] in the fifteenth year from the destruction; then was the Jubilee.

notes.he: אמר רבינא לעולם בחד בשבא חרב ודקא קשיא לך לא איקלע יובל עד ט"ו תריץ הכי י"ד שנה אחר שנה שהוכתה דהוו להו ט"ו בהדי ההוא שנה שהוכתה]:
notes.en: Ravina said: Actually it was destroyed in the first of the cycle; and as for your difficulty that the Jubilee would not arrive until the fifteenth, explain it thus: fourteen years after the year it was smitten, which makes fifteen together with that year in which it was smitten.]

messages.text: If so, when the verse states that Ezekiel’s prophecy fourteen years after the destruction of the Temple was in the twenty-fifth year of captivity, that is not precise; it was actually the twenty-sixth year of captivity.
messages.quote: in the fourteenth year after the year that the city was smitten

notes.he: דבשנת ט"ו לחורבן הוי ההיא נבואה כ"ו לגלות יהויכין הואי:
notes.en: If so: that this prophecy was in the fifteenth year from the destruction, it was the twenty-sixth of the exile of Jehoiachin.

notes.he: דהוה שנת ט"ו לחורבן עשרין וה' הויין כ"ו הויין דאמר מר גלו בז' פי' בז' לכיבוש יהויקים שכיבש בד' למלכותו והוא מלך י"א שנה ובאותה שנה הרג יהויקים והמליך יהויכין בנו ג' חדשים ולתקופת השנה באותה שנה הגלהו לבבל והחרש והמסגר ואז היה גלות דיחזקאל:
notes.en: If so: that it was the fifteenth year from the destruction, then the twenty-five are twenty-six. As the Master says: They were exiled in the seventh, meaning, in the seventh from the subjugation of Jehoiakim, whom he subjugated in the fourth year of his [Jehoiakim’s] reign. And he [Jehoiakim] reigned eleven years, and in that year he [Nebuchadnezzar] killed Jehoiakim and crowned his son Jehoiachin for three months; and at the turn of the year, in that same year, he exiled him to Babylonia, together with the craftsmen and the smiths. That was the exile of Ezekiel.

notes.he: אי הכי כיון דחשבת י"ד בר מההיא שתא דחרוב:
notes.en: If so: since you count fourteen apart from that year in which it was destroyed,

notes.he: עשרין ושית הוויין והא כתיב בכ"ה שנה:
notes.en: it comes to twenty-six, yet it is written “in the twenty-fifth year.”

messages.text: The Jews were exiled first in Nebuchadnezzar’s seventh year, and they were also exiled first in Nebuchadnezzar’s eighth year. This first exile took place during Nebuchadnezzar’s eighth year counting from the beginning of his reign; it was Nebuchadnezzar’s seventh year counting from the year he subjugated Jehoiakim, king of Judah.

notes.he: ישראל עם יהויכין:
notes.en: As the Master says: They were exiled: Israel, with Jehoiachin.

notes.he: בשנה שביעית לכיבוש יהויקים:
notes.en: In the seventh: in the seventh year from the subjugation of Jehoiakim.

notes.he: כלומר שאותה גלות היתה בשנה שמינית למלכות נבוכדנצר דשנה שניה למלכותו כיבש יהויקים כדמפרש לקמן:
notes.en: They were exiled in the eighth: that is, that same exile was in the eighth year of Nebuchadnezzar’s reign, since he subjugated Jehoiakim in the second year of his reign, as is explained below.

messages.text: They were then exiled a second time in Nebuchadnezzar’s eighteenth year, and they were exiled in Nebuchadnezzar’s nineteenth year, when the Temple was destroyed. This statement will be explained later.

notes.he: עם צדקיהו והיא היתה חרבות ירושלים והיא היתה שנת י"ח לכיבוש יהויקים והיא שנת י"ט לנבוכדנצר:
notes.en: They were exiled in the eighteenth: with Zedekiah, and that was the destruction of Jerusalem; and that was the eighteenth year from the subjugation of Jehoiakim, which is the nineteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar.

notes.he: גלו בי"ח לכיבוש היינו כשהוכתה העיר:
notes.en: They were exiled in the eighteenth from the subjugation: that is, when the city was smitten.

notes.he: דאמר מר גלו בז' גלו בח' לאחר ז' שנים שגלה יהויקים גלה (דגלה) יחזקאל [עם] יכניה [גלו בי"ח לאחר גלות יהויקים גלו עם צדקיהו וחרב הבית]:
notes.en: As the Master says: They were exiled in the seventh, they were exiled in the eighth: seven years after Jehoiakim was exiled, Ezekiel was exiled [with] Jeconiah. [They were exiled in the eighteenth after the exile of Jehoiakim: they were exiled with Zedekiah, and the Temple was destroyed.]

messages.text: Now, from the seventh year, when the first exile occurred, until the eighteenth year, when the second exile occurred, in conjunction with the Temple’s destruction, is eleven years, not counting the year of the destruction, and an additional fifteen years, until the date mentioned in the verse in Ezekiel, equals twenty-six years from the first exile, not twenty-five.

notes.he: משנה שביעית שהוא גלות יחזקאל עד תמני סרי שהוא חורבן הבית חד סרי לבהדי שתא דגלה בה יחזקאל ולבר משנת החורבן דמנינו לה בהדי הנך דמחורבן ועד יובל וחמיסר דמחורבן ועד יובל עם שנת החורבן ושנת היובל אשתכח דכ"ו הוו מהשתא דגלו בה ועד יובל והיכי אמר יחזקאל בעשרים וחמש לגלותנו היה יובל וס"ד דבהדי שתא דגלו קאמר:
notes.en: From seven until eighteen: from the seventh year, which is the exile of Ezekiel, until eighteen, which is the destruction of the Temple, is eleven, counting the year in which Ezekiel was exiled and not counting the year of the destruction, which we counted with those from the destruction until the Jubilee; and fifteen from the destruction until the Jubilee, with the year of the destruction and the Jubilee year. It turns out there were twenty-six from the year in which they were exiled until the Jubilee; so how did Ezekiel say that the Jubilee was in the twenty-fifth of our captivity? For it was assumed that he means counting together with the year in which they were exiled.

notes.dh: משבע שגלו בה עד תמניסר שחרבה העיר
notes.he: בלא תמניסר עצמו שהוא מנין דט"ו חדסר דשנה שביעית שגלו בה היא היתה שנה אחרונה ליהויקים ושוב מלך צדקיהו י' שנים לפני שנת החורבן וט"ו כ"ו הויין בשלמא אי אמרינן די"ד שנה לחורבן עצמו קאמר ניחא די"ד וי"א הם כ"ה אלא כיון דאמר דהוה שנת ט"ו קשיא ומצית לשנויי דשנה שגלו בה היא היתה שנה ראשונה לצדקיהו וליכא אלא י' שנים מן הגלות עד שנת של חורבן אלא קים ליה דאינו כן דהגלות היה באותה שנה שנמנית ליהויקים א"כ איכא אחד עשר שנה:
notes.en: From the seventh, in which they were exiled, until the eighteenth, in which the city was destroyed, not counting the eighteenth itself, which belongs to the count of fifteen, is eleven: for the seventh year, in which they were exiled, was the last year of Jehoiakim, and then Zedekiah reigned ten years before the year of the destruction; and with fifteen, that makes twenty-six. Granted, had we said that the fourteen years are counted with the year of the destruction itself, it would work out, since fourteen and eleven are twenty-five; but since he says it was the fifteenth year, it is difficult. One could have answered that the year in which they were exiled was the first year of Zedekiah, so there are only ten years from the exile to the year of the destruction; but he holds as established that this is not so, for the exile was in the very year that is counted for Jehoiakim. If so, there are eleven years.

notes.he: כשגלה יכניה ועד י"ח כשחרב הבית י"א שנה וט"ו כדאוקמת אחר שנה שהוכתה העיר דהיינו כ"ו וקרא אמר בכ"ה לגלותנו אלא ודאי י"ד הוו ותו לא דהוה להו כ"ה שנים. אמר לך רבינא ולדידך דתריצת הכי בי"ד מי ניחא דליהוו כ"ה שנים ותו לא מיכדי גלו [נמי] בי"ט ובעל כורחיך הוי כ"ו אלא מאי אית לך למימר דליהוו כ"ה ותו לא לבר משתא דגלו בה דלא חשיב [דבצר] ההיא שנת י"ט דגלו אלא י"ח ולא הוו אלא י"א וי"ד דהוו כ"ה:
notes.en: From seven, when Jeconiah was exiled, until eighteen, when the Temple was destroyed, is eleven years; and fifteen, as you established, “after the year the city was smitten,” makes twenty-six; yet the verse says “in the twenty-fifth of our captivity.” Rather, certainly there were fourteen and no more, making twenty-five years. Ravina could say to you: And according to you, who answered thus, “in the fourteenth,” does it work out that there are twenty-five years and no more? Now, they were [also] exiled in the nineteenth, and perforce it makes twenty-six. Rather, what have you to say, so that it makes twenty-five and no more? Separate from the year in which they were exiled, which is not counted, [so that you subtract] that nineteenth year in which they were exiled, leaving only eighteen; and there are only eleven and fourteen, which make twenty-five.

messages.text: And according to you, who maintains that the fourteen years mentioned in the verse include the year of the destruction of the Temple, does it work out well? Now, they were also exiled in the nineteenth year, and it was then that the Temple was destroyed. From the seventh year until the nineteenth year is twelve years, and an additional fourteen years until the date mentioned in the verse in Ezekiel equals twenty-six years from the first exile, not twenty-five.
messages.lead: The Gemara explains that Ravina could have said to you:

notes.he: דבעית למימני לשנת החורבן בהנך ארבעה עשר מי ניחא:
notes.en: And according to you: who wants to count the year of the destruction among these fourteen, does it work out well?

notes.he: דס"ד דהאי מתרץ דג' גליות הוו דהא דתני גלו בי"ח ובי"ט הוו שני גליות וסבר דבשמונה עשר הוה חורבן וכי מנית נמי ארביסר לבהדי שנת חורבן ושנת היובל משכחת לה עשרין ושית בגלות יהויכין שהיתה בשנת שבע ולבהדי שתא דגלו בה:
notes.en: Now, they were also exiled in the nineteenth: for this answerer had assumed that there were three exiles, since what is taught, “they were exiled in the eighteenth” and “in the nineteenth,” were two exiles, and he held that the destruction was in the eighteenth. And when you count fourteen as well, together with the year of the destruction and the Jubilee year, you find twenty-six from the exile of Jehoiachin, which was in the seventh year, counting together with the year in which they were exiled.

notes.he: מכדי גלו בי"ט שנה והיינו כשהוכתה העיר מז' עד י"ט י"ב הוו וארבסרי כ"ו הויין ומצי למיפרך לפי שיטתן שהיה סבור די"ח וי"ט שני גליות דא"כ היכי מתוקמא אי הוכתה בי"ח לא הוכתה בי"ט ואין להקפיד דסוגיא בעלמא הוא ולמסקנא ניחא:
notes.en: And according to you, does it work out well? Now, they were exiled in the nineteenth year, and that is when the city was smitten: from seven to nineteen is twelve, and with fourteen that makes twenty-six. He could have objected according to their own approach, since he thought that the eighteenth and the nineteenth were two exiles: if so, how can it be explained? If it was smitten in the eighteenth, it was not smitten in the nineteenth. But one need not be particular, since it is merely the course of the discussion, and by the conclusion it works out.

messages.text: Rather, what have you to say? That the twenty-five years are counted separate from the year when they were exiled for the first time. According to my opinion also, I can say that the twenty-five years are separate from the year when they were exiled for the first time.

notes.he: האי דקאמר יחזקאל בעשרים וחמש לגלותנו:
notes.en: Rather, what have you to say: about what Ezekiel says, “in the twenty-fifth year of our captivity”?

notes.he: יהויכין ויחזקאל:
notes.en: Separate from the year when they were exiled: Jehoiachin and Ezekiel.

notes.he: קא חשיב י"ד לבר מההיא שתא דגלו בה דמטפי לה כדאמרן:
notes.en: According to me too: he counts fourteen apart from that year in which they were exiled, which he adds, as we said.

messages.text: In any case, the assertion of the baraita that the destruction of the Temple occurred in the nineteenth year is difficult for Ravina, because there are eleven years from the first exile until the year of the destruction, not counting the year of the exile or the year of the destruction, and then an additional fifteen years, including the year of the destruction, until the date mentioned in the verse in Ezekiel, which is a total of twenty-six years, not twenty-five.
messages.quote: they were exiled in Nebuchadnezzar’s nineteenth year, when the Temple was destroyed

notes.he: דהא ודאי בגלות האחרון היה החורבן וכיון דאמר רבינא חמיסרי שנים עד היובל ומגלות יהויכין ועד שנת חורבן שהוא בי"ט הוו חד סרי לבר משתא דגלו בה ולבר שנת החורבן וחמיסרי הא עשרין ושית:
notes.en: In any case, the nineteenth is difficult for Ravina: for certainly the destruction was at the last exile. And since Ravina said fifteen years until the Jubilee, and from the exile of Jehoiachin until the year of the destruction, which is in the nineteenth, there are eleven, not counting the year in which they were exiled and not counting the year of the destruction, then with the fifteen, that makes twenty-six.

notes.he: מ"מ גלו בי"ט לרבינא קשיא דאי חשיב משב ועד י"ט י"ב ולבתר הכי י"ד הויין כ"ו דרבינא מטפי:
notes.en: In any case, “they were exiled in the nineteenth” is difficult for Ravina: for if he counts from seven to nineteen, that is twelve, and after that fourteen, making twenty-six, since Ravina adds [a year].

messages.text: Do you hold that there were three separate exiles, one in the seventh or eighth year, a second one in the eighteenth year, and a third one in the nineteenth year?

notes.he: הש"ס הוא דקא מתרץ דהאי דאמרן לעיל גלו נמי בתישסרי לאו מלתא היא דחד גלות הוה דבשמונה עשר לכיבוש יהויקים הוו חרבות ירושלים שהיא תשעה עשר לנבוכדנצר הלכך משב ועד תשעה עשר לבר משתא דגלו בה יהויכין ויחזקאל ולבר שנת החורבן וט"ו עם שנת החורבן ושנת היובל הרי כ"ה:
notes.en: Do you hold there were three exiles: it is the Talmud that answers that what we said above, “they were also exiled in the nineteenth,” is not so, for it was one exile: in the eighteenth from the subjugation of Jehoiakim was the destruction of Jerusalem, which is the nineteenth of Nebuchadnezzar. Therefore, from seven until nineteen, not counting the year in which Jehoiachin and Ezekiel were exiled and not counting the year of the destruction, and fifteen with the year of the destruction and the Jubilee year, makes twenty-five.

notes.he: אמר לך רבינא מי סברת ג' גליות הואי האי דקאמר משב ועד י"ח ומשב ועד י"ט לא הוו אלא שתי גליות דהאי דקאמר גלו בז' גלו בח' היינו חדא שתא וכן נמי גלו בי"ח גלו בי"ט חדא שתא והאי דקאמר [ליה מי סברת] ג' גליות ולא אמר ד' גליות משום דאיהו לא קא איירי בח' אלא משב ועד י"ח ומשב ועד י"ט קאמר הלכך קאמר ליה מי סברת ג' גליות גלו:
notes.en: Ravina could say to you: Do you hold there were three exiles? As for what he says, “from seven until eighteen” and “from seven until nineteen,” there were only two exiles: what he says, “they were exiled in the seventh, they were exiled in the eighth,” is one year, and likewise “they were exiled in the eighteenth, they were exiled in the nineteenth” is one year. And the reason he says to him “[do you hold] three exiles” and not “four exiles” is that he was not dealing with the eighth, but said “from seven until eighteen” and “from seven until nineteen.” Therefore he says to him: Do you hold there were three exiles?

messages.text: In truth there were only two exiles: They were exiled in the seventh year from Nebuchadnezzar’s subjugation of Jehoiakim, which was the eighth year of Nebuchadnezzar’s reign. They were then exiled a second time, when the Temple was destroyed, in the eighteenth year from the subjugation of Jehoiakim, which was actually in the nineteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar’s reign.

notes.he: גלות [יהויכין] בשבע לכיבוש יהויקים שהיא שמינית [למלכות] נבוכדנצר וגלו בגלות צדקיהו בי"ח לכיבוש יהויקים שהיא י"ט לנבוכדנצר ולא הוו אלא ב' גליות ובין גלות (יהויקים) [יהויכין] לגלות צדקיה לא הוו אלא י"א שנה:
notes.en: The exile [of Jehoiachin] was in the seventh from the subjugation of Jehoiakim, which is the eighth [of the reign] of Nebuchadnezzar; and they were exiled in the exile of Zedekiah in the eighteenth from the subjugation of Jehoiakim, which is the nineteenth of Nebuchadnezzar. So there were only two exiles, and between the exile of (Jehoiakim) [Jehoiachin] and the exile of Zedekiah there were only eleven years.

messages.text: Consequently, there were eleven years from the first exile to the destruction of the Temple, not counting the year of the exile, and another fourteen years until the verse in Ezekiel, which equals a total of twenty-five years.
The Gemara corroborates its interpretation of the baraita.
In the first year of his reign, Nebuchadnezzar conquered Nineveh;

notes.he: בסדר עולם:
notes.en: As the Master says: in Seder Olam.

messages.text: in his second year he ascended to Eretz Yisrael and conquered Jehoiakim.

notes.he: לאו גלות הוא דלא הגלה שום אדם אלא כבשו לעבד תחתיו ועבדו שלש שנים כדכתיב (מלכים ב כ״ד:א׳) ויהי לו יהויקים עבד שלש שנים וישב וימרד בו ג' שנים כדכתיב בדניאל בתחלתו בשנת שלש למלכות יהויקים (עלה) נבוכדנצר ירושלים ותניא בסדר עולם אפשר לומר כן והלא לא מלך נבוכד נצר עד שנה רביעית ליהויקים כדכתיב (בירמיהו כ״ה:א׳) הדבר אשר היה על ירמיהו על כל עם יהודה בשנה הרביעית ליהויקים היא השנה הראשונית לנבוכד נצר אם כן מה תלמוד לומר בשנת שלש למרדו שהיא ששית לכיבושו והילוכו לבבל והמליך יהויכין תחתיו וכתיב בסוף דברי הימים ולתשובת השנה וגו' אלמא בשנת שבע לכיבוש ראשון של יהויקים גלה יהויכין וכתיב בסוף מלכים ויצא אליו יהויכין מלך יהודה וגו' אלמא שביעית לכיבוש יהויקים היא שמינית למלכות נבוכד נצר והיינו דאמרי' שנה שניה כיבש יהויקים:
notes.en: He subjugated Jehoiakim: this was not an exile, for he exiled no one; rather, he subjugated him to serve under him. And he served him three years, as it is written (II Kings 24:1): “And Jehoiakim became his servant three years”; and he then rebelled against him for three years. As it is written at the beginning of Daniel: “In the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim … Nebuchadnezzar [came] to Jerusalem.” And it is taught in Seder Olam: Is it possible to say so? But Nebuchadnezzar did not become king until the fourth year of Jehoiakim, as it is written (Jeremiah 25:1): “The word that came to Jeremiah concerning all the people of Judah in the fourth year of Jehoiakim … that was the first year of Nebuchadnezzar.” If so, what does “in the third year” teach? The third year of his rebellion, which is the sixth of his subjugation; and his going to Babylonia, and he crowned Jehoiachin in his place. And it is written at the end of Chronicles: “And at the return of the year,” and so on. Evidently, in the seventh year from the first subjugation of Jehoiakim, Jehoiachin was exiled. And it is written at the end of Kings: “And Jehoiachin king of Judah went out to him,” and so on [in the eighth year of his reign]. Evidently, the seventh from the subjugation of Jehoiakim is the eighth of Nebuchadnezzar’s reign. And that is why we say: in the second year he subjugated Jehoiakim.

messages.caption: Two exiles, counted two ways: the seventh and eighteenth years from the subjugation of Jehoiakim are Nebuchadnezzar’s eighth and nineteenth, and eleven years plus fourteen make Ezekiel’s twenty-fifth year of captivity.

messages.text: § The Gemara continues its discussion of the baraita, which teaches:

When the Temple was destroyed for the first time, that day was the Ninth of Av; and it was the conclusion of Shabbat; and it was the year after a Sabbatical Year; and likewise, the same happened when the Second Temple was destroyed.

notes.he: [וכן בשניה בחורבן בית שני גלו במוצאי שביעית ובמוצאי שבת:
notes.en: [And likewise in the Second: at the destruction of the Second Temple, they were exiled in the year after a Sabbatical Year and at the conclusion of Shabbat.

messages.text: Can you find such a possibility, that the Second Temple was destroyed in the year after a Sabbatical Year? Now, for how many years did the Second Temple stand? It stood for 420 years.
messages.quote: and likewise, the same happened when the Second Temple was destroyed

notes.he: שלמין לבד שנה שחרב בו:
notes.en: Four hundred and twenty: complete, apart from the year in which it was destroyed.

messages.text: Four hundred years include exactly eight Jubilees, as the Jubilee cycle is fifty years. An additional fourteen years consist of two Sabbatical cycles. There are six years remaining during which the Temple stood, which means that the last year was the sixth year of the Sabbatical cycle, and therefore when the Temple was destroyed the following year it was a Sabbatical Year, not the year after the Sabbatical Year.

notes.he: כלו ת"כ שנים ובשביעית עצמה חרב:
notes.en: It was the sixth of the Sabbatical cycle: the 420 years were completed, and it was destroyed in the Sabbatical Year itself.

notes.he: פי' דמנין ת"כ שנים כלה בשית בשבוע והחורבן היה בשנת כ"א דהכי מוכחא סוגיא דלא חרב הבית בשניה עד שנת כ"א ובית ראשון שעמד ת"י שנים חרב בשנת עשר עצמו הכי מוכח כל הסוגיא נמצא בית חרב בתחילת יובל כלומר בשנת יובל עצמה דהחורבן בשנת ת"י. רש"י:
notes.en: It was the sixth of the cycle: meaning, the count of 420 years ended in the sixth of the cycle, and the destruction was in year 421. For so the passage shows, that the Second [Temple] was not destroyed until year 421; whereas the First Temple, which stood 410 years, was destroyed in year 410 itself, as the whole passage shows. It turns out the Temple was destroyed at the beginning of the Jubilee, that is, in the Jubilee Year itself, since the destruction was in year 410. [So] Rashi.

messages.text: In accordance with whose opinion is this baraita stated? It is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda,

The fiftieth year is counted for here and for there, i.e., it is both the Jubilee Year and the first year of the next Sabbatical cycle and Jubilee cycle, and therefore each Jubilee cycle is only forty-nine years rather than fifty years.

notes.he: לשנת יובל והיא תחילת יובל הבא הלכך לר' יהודה לא הוי בכל יובל אלא מ"ט שנים:
notes.en: The fiftieth year counts: for the Jubilee Year, and it is the beginning of the next Jubilee. Therefore, according to Rabbi Yehuda, each Jubilee has only forty-nine years.

notes.he: ליובל ולמנותה שנה ראשונה של שבוע הבא:
notes.en: Counts for here and for there: for the Jubilee, and to be counted as the first year of the next cycle.

messages.text: Consequently, when calculating the number of years of the Sabbatical and Jubilee cycles until the destruction of the Second Temple, bring an additional eight years from the eight complete Jubilee cycles during which the Temple stood. The eight years and those six years that remained according to the previous calculation equal fourteen years, which are two complete Sabbatical cycles. Therefore, it is found that the Second Temple was destroyed in the year following the Sabbatical Year.

But if one explains the baraita in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda, the first clause of the baraita is problematic, as you do not find that the first time the Temple was destroyed was in the year after the Sabbatical Year.

notes.he: מוקמת לה להא דר' יוסי בראשונה לא משכחת דחרב בית ראשון במוצאי שביעית:
notes.en: If like Rabbi Yehuda: you explain this statement of Rabbi Yosei, then regarding the First, you do not find that the First Temple was destroyed in the year after a Sabbatical Year.

notes.he: מוקמת לה בראשונה לא משכחת לה לטעמא דחרב במוצאי שביעית:
notes.en: If like Rabbi Yehuda you explain it, then regarding the First you do not find it, according to the reasoning that it was destroyed in the year after a Sabbatical Year.

messages.text: The Jewish people counted seventeen Jubilees from when they entered Eretz Yisrael until they left, when the First Temple was destroyed.

notes.he: נפקי מקראי דכתיב (מלכים א ו׳:א׳) ויהי בשמונים שנה וארבע מאות שנה וגו' דל ארבעים דמדבר אשתכח דנכנסו לארץ קודם בנין הבית ארבע מאות וארבעים ובית ראשון עמד ת"י הרי תת"נ הרי י"ז יובלות של חמשים:
notes.en: Seventeen Jubilees: this comes from the verses, as it is written (I Kings 6:1): “And it came to pass in the four hundred and eightieth year…” Subtract the forty of the wilderness, and it turns out that they entered the land 440 years before the building of the Temple; and the First Temple stood 410. That makes 850, which is seventeen Jubilees of fifty.

messages.text: And you cannot say that they counted from the time they entered, because if you say this, the result is that the Temple was destroyed at the beginning of the Jubilee cycle, and you do not find that the Jubilee Year was “in the fourteenth year after the city was smitten.”

verse.he: בְּעֶשְׂרִים וְחָמֵשׁ שָׁנָה לְגָלוּתֵנוּ בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה בֶּעָשׂוֹר לַחֹדֶשׁ בְּאַרְבַּע עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה אַחַר אֲשֶׁר הֻכְּתָה הָעִיר בְּעֶצֶם ׀ הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה הָיְתָה עָלַי יַד־יְהֹוָה וַיָּבֵא אֹתִי שָׁמָּה׃
verse.en: In the twenty-fifth year of our exile, the fourteenth year after the city had fallen, at the beginning of the year, the tenth day of the month—on that very day—GOD’s hand came upon me, and it brought me there.

notes.dh: ואי אתה יכול לומר משעה שנכנסו
notes.he: לארץ מנו שמיטין ויובלות דא"כ בית חרב בתחילת היובל כלומר בשנת היובל עצמה דהא ליכא למימר שלא חרב עד חמשים ואחת דא"כ לא מיתוקמא שמעתין דכי מדלית שבע שכיבשו ושבע שחילקו משכחת חורבן בשנת ל"ז של יובל והיינו שניה לשמיטה ואנן בעינן במוצאי שביעית הלכך אתפרש לן האי תחילת היובל שנת היובל עצמה ואי אתה מוצא שיהא יובל בי"ד שנה אחרי אשר הוכתה העיר כדכתיב ביחזקאל (סי' מ):
notes.en: And you cannot say from the time they entered: the land they counted Sabbatical Years and Jubilees, for if so, the Temple was destroyed at the beginning of the Jubilee, that is, in the Jubilee Year itself. For one cannot say that it was not destroyed until the fifty-first [year], since then our passage would not hold: when you subtract the seven of conquest and the seven of division, you would find the destruction in year thirty-seven of the Jubilee, which is the second of the Sabbatical cycle, whereas we need the year after a Sabbatical Year. Therefore this “beginning of the Jubilee” is explained to us as the Jubilee Year itself. And you do not find that the Jubilee would be “fourteen years after the city was smitten,” as it is written in Ezekiel (40).

messages.text: Rather, remove from them the seven years when they conquered the land and the seven years when they divided the land, as they did not start counting the first Jubilee cycle until after those events. And you then find that the Jubilee Year was “in the fourteenth year after the city was smitten.”

notes.he: ולא מנו שמיטין ויובלות עד לאחר י"ד [ואי] אתה מוצא שנת היובל י"ד שנה אחר שהוכתה העיר וכדתריץ רבינא לעיל דכי מדלית י"ד מחמשים פשו להו תלתין ושית אשתכח דבשנת שלשים ושש חרב הבית והיא מוצאי לשביעית ושנת היובל בי"ד שנה לבד משנת החורבן ואי הך דר' יוסי לעיל אליבא דר' יהודה אייתי שבסר שנין משבסר יובלי שדי אהני כלומר שדינהו על היובלות ודל י"ד מהנך שבסרי לשבע שכיבשו וז' שחילקו פשו להו תלת אשתכח דבג' בשבוע חרוב:
notes.en: Remove from them the seven when they conquered, and so on: and they did not count Sabbatical Years and Jubilees until after fourteen [years]; [and so] you find the Jubilee Year fourteen years after the city was smitten, as Ravina explained above. For when you subtract fourteen from fifty, thirty-six remain; it turns out the Temple was destroyed in the thirty-sixth year, which is the year after a Sabbatical Year, and the Jubilee Year came fourteen years later, apart from the year of the destruction. But if this statement of Rabbi Yosei above follows Rabbi Yehuda, bring seventeen years from the seventeen Jubilees and add them, that is, throw them onto the Jubilees; subtract fourteen of these seventeen for the seven of conquest and the seven of division, and three remain. It turns out it was destroyed in the third of the Sabbatical cycle.

notes.dh: אלא צא מהם שבע שכיבשו וז' שחילקו
notes.he: וישאר ל"ו ובאותה שנה חרבה העיר דהוי מוצאי שביעי' ואי רבי יהודה אייתי שבסרי מי"ז יובלות הרי נ"ג שנה הוה ליה בתלתא בשבוע והוא הדין דמצי למיפרך לר' יהודה אם כן היכי משכחת קרא דיחזקאל היה בי"ד לחורבן:
notes.en: Rather, remove from them the seven when they conquered and the seven when they divided: and thirty-six remain, and in that year the city was destroyed, which is the year after a Sabbatical Year. But if it follows Rabbi Yehuda, bring seventeen from the seventeen Jubilees, which makes fifty-three years: it would be the third of the Sabbatical cycle. And by the same token he could have objected according to Rabbi Yehuda: if so, how do you find the verse in Ezekiel, that it was [the Jubilee] in the fourteenth from the destruction?

notes.he: דתניא י"ז יובלות מנו ישראל משנכנסו לארץ ועד שיצאו דכתיב ויהי בשמנים שנה וארבע מאות שנה לצאת בני ישראל מארץ מצרים וגו' צא מהם מ' שנה שהיו במדבר נשארו ת"מ ועמד הבית ת"י הרי י"ז יובלות נמצא בית חרב בתחלת יובל י"ח ואי אתה מוצא לחשבון זה שבי"ד שנה אחר שהוכתה העיר שהיה יובל כמו שאמר בר"ה בעשור וגו' אלא צא מהם ז' שכיבשו וז' שחילקו כדמפרש לקמן דלא מנו ליובלות אלא לאחר י"ד שנכנסו לארץ ואתה מוצא י"ד אחר שהוכתה העיר דהוה יובל:
notes.en: As it is taught: Israel counted seventeen Jubilees from when they entered the land until they left, as it is written: “And it came to pass in the four hundred and eightieth year after the children of Israel came out of the land of Egypt,” and so on. Remove from them the forty years that they were in the wilderness, and 440 remain; and the Temple stood 410: that makes seventeen Jubilees. It turns out the Temple was destroyed at the beginning of the eighteenth Jubilee, and by this calculation you do not find that in the fourteenth year after the city was smitten it was a Jubilee, as it says, “at the beginning of the year, on the tenth,” and so on. Rather, remove from them the seven when they conquered and the seven when they divided, as is explained below, that they counted Jubilees only from fourteen years after they entered the land; and then you find that fourteen [years] after the city was smitten it was a Jubilee.

messages.text: But if one holds in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda, that each Jubilee cycle is forty-nine years rather than fifty years, you must bring an additional seventeen years, one from each of the seventeen Jubilee cycles and add them to these seventeen cycles, and it turns out that the destruction of the Temple was in the third year of the Sabbatical cycle.

notes.he: דאמר שנת נ' עולה לכאן ולכאן אייתי שבסרי משבסרי יובל ועייל י"ד מנייהו כנגד י"ד שכיבשו ושחילקו פשו להו תלתא שני אישתכח דבתלת בשבוע חרב ואי אתה מוצא נמי דלאחר י"ד לחורבנו היה יובל]:
notes.en: And if it follows Rabbi Yehuda, who says the fiftieth year counts for here and for there: bring seventeen from the seventeen Jubilees and set fourteen of them against the fourteen in which they conquered and divided. Three years remain; it turns out it was destroyed in the third of the cycle, and you also do not find that fourteen [years] after its destruction was a Jubilee.]

messages.text: Throughout those years from when Sennacherib exiled the ten tribes until Jeremiah came and returned them to their land, they did not count the Jubilee cycle, as the Jubilee applies only when all twelve tribes are in their ancestral lands. When the exiles returned, a new Jubilee cycle was started, and the Temple was destroyed thirty-six years later, in the year after a Sabbatical Year.

notes.dh: ומשני הנך תלת שנין דאגלינהו סנחריב עד דאתא ירמיה ואהדרינהו כו'
notes.he: כלומר הנך שלש שנים שצר סנחריב עליהן כדכתיב (במלכים ב י״ז:ה׳) ויעל מלך אשור (על כל) [בכל] הארץ ויעל שומרון ויצר עליה שלש שנים ולא היה להם פנאי לחרוש ולזרוע ולא מנו שמיטין ויובלות לא קא חשיב להו. והאי דנקט עד דאתא ירמיהו אהדרינהו לאו דווקא דהא יותר מתשעים שנה היה מחזקיהו שהגלה אותן סנחריב עד שהחזירן ירמיהו בימי יאשיהו אלא ה"ק תלת שני דאגלינהו סנחריב והיו באותו גלות עד שהחזירן ירמיהו לא חשיב להו להנך שלש שנים כך שמעתי. והרבה תשובות בדבר חדא דכי מדלית תלת שני משכחת חורבן בשנת ארבעים ותשע והיא שביעית ואנן בעינן מוצאי שביעית ועוד י"ד שנה אחרי אשר הוכתה העיר דליהוי יובל לא משכחת לה והא ליכא למימר לר' יהודה לית ליה הך דרשא דהא קרא כתיב ולקמן לא משכחינן ז' שחילקו אלא מהך דרשא די"ד אחרי אשר הוכתה העיר הוה יובל ועוד קשיא לי היכי לא מדלינן אלא הנך תלת שני והאמרי' בפ' בתרא (לקמן ערכין לב:) משגלו שבט ראובן וגד בטלו היובלות עד שהחזירן ירמיהו ואע"ג דמתרצינן התם מנו יובלות לקדש שמיטין הני מילי לרבנן אבל לר' יהודה מוקמינן התם דלא מנו יובלות כלל ועוד היאך יתכן ליטול שלש שנים לבדם אם כשעלה סנחריב עליהם כבר מנו י' שנים או י"ב ליובל ועלה עליהם שלש שנים היאך יתכן להפסיק אותן שלש שנים ולחזור למניינם הראשון ולמנות י"ג י"ד לקדש יובל שנת החמשים ושלש בעל כרחך אז התחילו למנות א' ב' ג' ד'. ומתוך הוויות אלו נראה בעיני דהאי תלת דכתב בספרים שיבוש הוא ופירוש משובש היה ונכתב בספרים. והכי גרסינן הנך שני דאגלינהו סנחריב עד דאתא ירמיהו אהדרינהו לא חשיב ודוקא נקט דכל אותן השנים שהיו בגלות לא חשיב רבי יהודה במנין שמיטין ויובלות וכדאמרי' בפרק בתרא אלא באותה שנה שחזרו בימי יאשיהו התחילו למנות ליובל וצא וחשוב מאותה שנה עד שנת הת"י החורבן ותמצא חשבונך סדור כמין חומר דבשנת שלשים ושש ליובל חרב הבית והיא מוצאי שביעית ומשכחת ארבע עשרה שנה אחר אשר הוכתה העיר הוה שנת היובל שהרי חזרו בשנת י"ח ליאשיהו כדכתיב (במלכים ב כ״ב:י״ג) דבשנת י"ח ליאשיהו נמצא הספר בבית המקדש ועל דברי הספר שלח המלך אל חולדה הנביאה ואמרי' במגילה (דף יד:) היכי שבקיה לירמיהו ושדר לחולדה ואמרינן ירמיה לא הוה התם שהלך להחזיר עשרת השבטים ומנלן דהדור דכתיב מה הציון הלז וגו' ודבר זה שפינה יאשיה את העבודת כוכבים באותה שנה היה וכך מצאתי בסדר עולם בי"ח ליאשיהו היה תחלת היובל ויאשיהו מלך ל"א שנה מי"ח עד ל"א כמה הוו ארבסרי וחד סרי ליהויקים ויהויכין וחד סרי לצדקיהו כדכתיב (במלכים ב כ״ה:כ״ז) הרי שלשים ושש ואז חרב הבית ומיתוקמא שפיר כר' יהודה. כך הבנתי מלבי וישרה בעיני אבל לא שמעתיה ואחרי כן מצאתי ספר ישן מוגה שכתוב בו כן והודעתיו לרבותי וישרה בעיניהם:
notes.en: [Rashi’s text first reads “those three years”; at the end he argues that “three” is a corruption, and the Davidson English follows the reading he adopts.] And he answers: Those three years from when Sennacherib exiled them until Jeremiah came and returned them, and so on: that is, those three years in which Sennacherib besieged them, as it is written (II Kings 17:5): “Then the king of Assyria came up throughout all the land, and went up to Samaria, and besieged it three years.” They had no opportunity to plow and sow and did not count Sabbatical Years and Jubilees, so he does not count them. And what it says, “until Jeremiah came and returned them,” is not precise, for it was more than ninety years from Hezekiah, when Sennacherib exiled them, until Jeremiah returned them in the days of Josiah. Rather, this is what it means: the three years in which Sennacherib exiled them, and they remained in that exile until Jeremiah returned them; those three years are not counted. So I heard. But there are many objections to this. First, when you subtract three years, you find the destruction in year forty-nine, which is a Sabbatical Year, whereas we need the year after a Sabbatical Year; and further, you do not find that fourteen years after the city was smitten was a Jubilee. And one cannot say that Rabbi Yehuda does not accept this exposition, for it is an explicit verse; and below, we find the seven years of division only from this exposition, that fourteen [years] after the city was smitten was a Jubilee. Further, it is difficult for me: why do we subtract only those three years? Don’t we say in the last chapter (below, Arakhin 32b): Once the tribe of Reuben and Gad were exiled, the Jubilees ceased, until Jeremiah returned them? And although we answer there that they counted Jubilees in order to sanctify the Sabbatical Years, that is only according to the Rabbis; but according to Rabbi Yehuda we establish there that they did not count Jubilees at all. Further, how is it possible to take out three years alone? If, when Sennacherib came up against them, they had already counted ten or twelve years of the Jubilee, and he came up against them for three years, how is it possible to skip those three years and return to their original count, and count thirteen, fourteen, to sanctify the Jubilee in the fifty-third year? Perforce they then began to count one, two, three, four. From all these considerations it seems to me that this “three” written in the books is an error, and a mistaken explanation was written into the books. This is how we read: “Those years from when Sennacherib exiled them until Jeremiah came and returned them are not counted,” and it is stated precisely: all those years that they were in exile, Rabbi Yehuda does not count in the count of Sabbatical Years and Jubilees, as we say in the last chapter. Rather, in the year when they returned, in the days of Josiah, they began to count for the Jubilee. Go and count from that year until year 410, the destruction, and you will find your calculation laid out neatly: in the thirty-sixth year of the Jubilee the Temple was destroyed, which is the year after a Sabbatical Year, and you find that fourteen years after the city was smitten was the Jubilee Year. For they returned in the eighteenth year of Josiah, as it is written (II Kings 22) that in the eighteenth year of Josiah the book was found in the Temple, and concerning the words of the book the king sent to Ḥulda the prophetess. And we say in Megilla (14b): How could he pass over Jeremiah and send to Ḥulda? And we say: Jeremiah was not there, for he had gone to bring back the ten tribes. And from where do we know that they returned? As it is written: “What is this monument,” and so on. And this matter, Josiah’s clearing away of idolatry, was in that year. And so I found in Seder Olam: in the eighteenth year of Josiah was the beginning of the Jubilee. Josiah reigned thirty-one years; from eighteen to thirty-one, how many are there? Fourteen; and eleven for Jehoiakim and Jehoiachin, and eleven for Zedekiah, as it is written (II Kings 25:27): that makes thirty-six, and then the Temple was destroyed. So it fits well according to Rabbi Yehuda. This I understood from my own heart, and it was right in my eyes, though I had not heard it [from my teachers]; and afterward I found an old, corrected book in which it is written so, and I told my teachers, and it was right in their eyes.

notes.he: ול"ג תלת שנים כי טובא הוו שהרי מששה לחזקיהו עד שבעה עשר ליאשיהו שהחזירם ירמיהו הוא קרוב למאה שנה ועוד הקשה רש"י על זה הלשון ושיבוש הוא:
notes.en: Those years in which Sennacherib exiled them: and we do not read “three years,” for there were many: from the sixth of Hezekiah until the seventeenth of Josiah, when Jeremiah returned them, is close to a hundred years. And Rashi further objected to this wording [with three], and it is an error.

notes.dh: הנך שני דאגלינהו סנחריב עד דאתא ירמיהו ואהדרינהו לא קחשיב
notes.he: והחזירם בי"ח ליאשיהו ומנה י"ד ליאשיהו דמלך ל"א וכ"ב דיהויקים וצדקיהו הרי ל"ו שנה ובשנת ל"ו חרבה וא"ת א"כ מאי קאמר בברייתא אם אתה אומר משנכנסו מנו נמצא בית חרב בתחילת יובל הא ליתא דכשגלו פסקו מלמנות יובלות וכשהחזירום החזירו למנות ולקדש ותו לא היה רק ל"ו שנה עד החורבן ואומר רבי דההיא ברייתא אתיא כרבנן דאמרי דשנת נ' אינו ממנין שמיטין ולדידהו כשגלו [נהי] נמי דלא מנו יובלות שמיטין מונין ומקדשין והיו מונין יובלות לקדש בו שמיטין דהכי איתא שילהי מכילתין לא מנו יובלות אלא לקדש שמיטין וא"כ כשהחזירום ירמיהו לא התחילו למנות תחילת היובל אלא לאותו חשבון עצמו שהיו מונין ולכך קאמר שאם מנו משנכנסו בית חרב בשנת יובל אבל לר' יהודה דאמר שנת נ' עצמו ממנין השמיטין ובשנים שגלו העשרת שבטים לא היו מונין שמיטין ולא יובלות כלל וא"כ כשהחזירם ירמיה ונהג יובל הוצרכו לחזור ולהתחיל מניינם:
notes.en: Those years from when Sennacherib exiled them until Jeremiah came and returned them are not counted: and he returned them in the eighteenth of Josiah. Count fourteen of Josiah, who reigned thirty-one, and twenty-two of Jehoiakim and Zedekiah: that makes thirty-six years, and in the thirty-sixth year it was destroyed. And if you ask: if so, what does the baraita mean, “If you say they counted from when they entered, the Temple turns out to have been destroyed at the beginning of the Jubilee”? That is not so, for when they were exiled they stopped counting Jubilees, and when they were returned they resumed counting and sanctifying, and there were only thirty-six years until the destruction. My teacher says that that baraita follows the Rabbis, who say that the fiftieth year is not part of the count of the Sabbatical cycles. According to them, when they were exiled, granted they did not count Jubilees, but they did count and sanctify Sabbatical Years, and they would count Jubilees in order to sanctify the Sabbatical Years by them, as it is at the end of our tractate: they counted Jubilees only to sanctify the Sabbatical Years. If so, when Jeremiah returned them, they did not begin counting from the start of a Jubilee, but continued the same count they had been counting. That is why it says that if they counted from when they entered, the Temple was destroyed in a Jubilee Year. But according to Rabbi Yehuda, who says the fiftieth year itself is part of the count of the Sabbatical cycles, in the years that the ten tribes were exiled they counted neither Sabbatical Years nor Jubilees at all; if so, when Jeremiah returned them and the Jubilee was in force, they had to start their count over.

notes.he: אפיק להו כנגד הנך תלת שני דאגלינהו סנחריב עד דאתא ירמיה ואהדרינהו (כדמתרגמינן) [כדגרסינן] בפירקין בתרא מלמד שירמיה החזירם דלא קא חשיב להו משום דלא הוו ישראל על אדמתם ולא מנו ליובלות עד שחזרו דכתיב וקראתם דרור בארץ לכל יושביה בזמן שכל יושביה עליה ואמר לן ר' דהאי דאגלינהו תלת שני לא אשכחן ליה בפירוש במקרא אלא סמכו על המקרא דכתיב [ויהי בשנה הרביעית למלך חזקיהו היא השנה השביעית להושע בן אלה מלך ישראל] עלה שלמנאסר מלך אשור על שומרון ויצר עליה וילכדה מקצה שלש שנים [בשנת שש לחזקיה] אישתכח דכי מפיק להני תלת שני דבמוצאי שביעית [חרב אבל אי אתה מוצא לאחר י"ד שנה יובל לטעמא דרבי יהודה:
notes.en: [Rabbeinu Gershom’s text reads “those three years”; the Davidson English, following the Vilna text, omits “three.”] Those three years: he takes them out, corresponding to those three years from when Sennacherib exiled them until Jeremiah came and returned them, (as we translate) [as we read] in the last chapter: this teaches that Jeremiah returned them. He does not count them because Israel was not on its land, and they did not count Jubilees until they returned, as it is written: “And proclaim liberty throughout the land unto all the inhabitants thereof”: when all its inhabitants are upon it. My teacher told us that these three years in which he exiled them we do not find explicitly in Scripture; rather, they relied on the verse that is written: “[And it came to pass in the fourth year of King Hezekiah, which was the seventh year of Hoshea son of Elah, king of Israel,] that Shalmaneser king of Assyria came up against Samaria and besieged it, and at the end of three years they took it, [in the sixth year of Hezekiah].” It turns out that when he takes out these three years, it was [destroyed] in the year after a Sabbatical Year; [but you do not find a Jubilee fourteen years later, according to Rabbi Yehuda’s reasoning.

messages.text: Some texts read “those three years” here, as Rabbeinu Gershom’s does. Rashi argues that “three” is a copyist’s error and Tosafot agree; the printed text and this translation read without it.

And if you wish, say instead: Actually, the baraita is in accordance with the opinion of the Rabbis, and when it teaches: And likewise, the same happened when the Second Temple was destroyed, it is not asserting that the Temple was destroyed in a year after a Sabbatical Year, because in fact the Second Temple was destroyed during a Sabbatical Year.
messages.quote: and likewise, the same happened when the Second Temple was destroyed

notes.he: אמרה ר' יוסי למילתיה ודקא קשיא לך לעיל הוה ליה בשיתא בשבוע:
notes.en: And if you wish, say: actually, according to the Rabbis, Rabbi Yosei stated his teaching; and as for your difficulty above, that it was the sixth of the cycle,

messages.text: Rather, it is referring to the other details the baraita provides with regard to the timing of the destruction, i.e., that it occurred on the Ninth of Av and on a Sunday.

notes.he: אתשעה באב ומוצאי שבת:
notes.en: when it teaches “and likewise for the Second,” it refers to the rest: to the Ninth of Av and the conclusion of Shabbat.

notes.he: מצית מוקמת לה וכן בשניה ודקא קשיא לך פש להו שית לאו אמוצאי שביעית אמרי וכן אלא אשארא בתשעה באב ובמוצאי שבת:
notes.en: If you wish, say: actually you can explain it according to the Rabbis, and “and likewise for the Second”: as for your difficulty that six remain, they did not say “and likewise” about the year after a Sabbatical Year, but about the rest: the Ninth of Av and the conclusion of Shabbat.

messages.caption: Was each Temple destroyed in the year after a Sabbatical Year? The count by the Rabbis’ fifty-year Jubilee and by Rabbi Yehuda’s forty-nine.

messages.text: So too, it is reasonable to conclude that not all of the details pertaining to the destruction of the First Temple also apply to the destruction of the Second Temple. As, if you do not say so, then with regard to the statement that the destruction occurred during the week of the priestly watch of Jehoiarib, was the priestly watch of Jehoiarib present during the time of the Second Temple?

notes.dh: משמרתו של יהויריב בשניה מי הואי
notes.he: הקשה רבינו אלחנן דהא אמרי' ב"ק (דף קי.) נתן הכסף לידעיה ואת האשם ליהויריב אלמא שהיה בבית שני ויש לומר דהא מתני' מיתניא סמוך לבית ראשון אי נמי לא יהויריב דווקא אלא המשמר תחת יהויריב:
notes.en: Was the watch of Jehoiarib present in the Second? Rabbeinu Elḥanan objected: But we say in Bava Kamma (110a): He gives the money to Jedaiah and the guilt offering to Jehoiarib; evidently it existed in the Second Temple. One can say that that mishna was taught with reference to the time close to the First Temple. Alternatively, not Jehoiarib precisely, but the watch in place of Jehoiarib.

messages.text: But isn’t it taught in a baraita that the watch of Jehoiarib did not exist during the Second Temple era? As it is taught:

Only four priestly watches ascended from the Babylonian exile, while the other twenty stayed in Babylonia. And these are the watches who returned: The descendants of Jedaiah, Harim, Pashḥur, and Immer.

notes.he: בימי עזרא:
notes.en: Ascended from the exile: in the days of Ezra.

notes.he: שבמקדש ראשון היתה משמרת ידעיה קודם לחרים ומשמרת חרים קודם לפשחור ושל פשחור לאימר:
notes.en: Jedaiah, Harim, Pashḥur and Immer: for in the First Temple the watch of Jedaiah came before Harim, the watch of Harim before Pashḥur, and that of Pashḥur before Immer.

notes.he: עם עזרא ותו לא]:
notes.en: Four watches ascended from the exile: with Ezra, and no more.]

messages.text: The prophets among those who returned arose and divided these four families into twenty-four watches.

notes.he: ולא היו יודעין כיצד יסדרן מי יעבוד אחר מי:
notes.en: Divided them into twenty-four watches: and they did not know how to order them, who would serve after whom.

messages.text: They achieved this as follows: They wrote the names of these new twenty-four watches on pieces of paper, mixed them up, and put them in a receptacle [kalpi] from which lots were drawn. A representative from the family of Jedaiah came and drew his portion and the lot of five other watches, for a total of six.

notes.he: שכתבו שם הכ"ד משמרות בכ"ד פתקין:
notes.en: Mixed them up: they wrote the names of the twenty-four watches on twenty-four slips.

notes.he: וכוון ידעיה ברוח הקודש ועלתה איגרתו בידו וחזר והכניס ידו ונטל איגרת וכן עד שש פעמים ובאותו סדר שעלו האיגרות בידו כך עשו אחריו אותן הכתובין באיגרות זו אחר זו:
notes.en: And put them in a receptacle: and Jedaiah directed [his hand] by the holy spirit, and his own slip came up in his hand; he put his hand in again and took a slip, and so on six times. And in the order in which the slips came up in his hand, so they set those written on the slips after him, one after another.

messages.text: Continues on 13a: Harim, Pashḥur and Immer each draw six lots in the same way, and the prophets stipulate that Jedaiah keeps its precedence even if Jehoiarib returns; so the baraita’s “likewise” must refer to the other details.
